column5: Biallelic BUB1B variants: a null or truncating allele in trans with a hypomorphic missense or regulatory allele
Kinetochore-microtubule attachment stability and chromosome congression via the BubR1 KARD-PP2A-B56 arm
Chromosome missegregation and mosaic variegated aneuploidy
p53- and p16-dependent arrest, senescence and immune clearance of missegregating cells
Intrauterine and postnatal growth restriction with microcephaly
Childhood cancer predisposition: embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms tumour and leukaemia

column18: Demonstrated for truncating alleles (transcripts absent) and for a 44 kb upstream regulatory allele introduced by genome editing. The residual transcript level produced by any particular allele pair is not predictable a priori.

Abundance is set by two independent processes whose relative contribution is allele-specific: absent transcript from the null allele, and accelerated turnover of the missense protein. Not all MVA alleles act this way: one published class produces a qualitative checkpoint or attachment defect at normal abundance.

The abundance threshold at which the complex fails has been mapped only in HeLa by graded shRNA knockdown, where aneuploidy appeared below roughly 50 percent residual BubR1. The threshold in the affected human tissues is unmeasured.
Established biochemistry of the checkpoint. The quantitative relationship between residual complex and residual anaphase delay in primary patient cells is not measured.

Demonstrated in cell lines by KARD-domain mutation and by BubR1 depletion. This arm is independent of the checkpoint arm, so the therapeutic target must be the protein rather than the checkpoint; how much of the patient phenotype each arm contributes is not separable with current data.
Premature chromatid separation is scored on fixed metaphase spreads, so its relationship to anaphase timing in living tissue is reconstructed rather than observed.

Graded knockdown shows premature chromatid separation appears at higher residual BubR1 than aneuploidy does, so the two are not interchangeable readouts and a drug could move one without moving the other.
Demonstrated in transformed cell lines. Whether attachment error contributes materially to missegregation in BUB1B-mutant primary human tissue has not been measured.

Demonstrated in engineered trisomic yeast, mouse and human cells. It has not been measured in BUB1B-mutant primary patient tissue, where the aneuploidies are mosaic and heterogeneous rather than a single defined trisomy.

Demonstrated in human cells and mouse models. Whether this response is on balance protective or pathological in this disease is genuinely contested: in BubR1-hypomorphic mice p16-driven senescence drives the progeroid phenotype, while the p53 arm suppresses aneuploidy-driven tumorigenesis. The node is therefore flagged compensatory so that no corrective direction is derived from it.

INFERRED. Aneuploidy-associated stress and the p53 response are each documented, but that the stress causes the clearance response, rather than both being parallel consequences of missegregation, has not been demonstrated.

INFERRED, and the weakest joint in this chain. That progenitor attrition rather than a cell-autonomous growth defect, or the separately reported ciliogenesis defect, is what produces growth restriction and microcephaly has not been demonstrated in human BUB1B-mutant tissue. Which tissues and which developmental windows dominate is unresolved.

Observed clinically in MVA cohorts. The relationship is non-monotonic in mouse models: low-rate missegregation promotes tumours while very high-rate missegregation suppresses them, and where BUB1B-MVA sits on that curve is not known. This is the reason an agent that increases missegregation cannot be assumed to be either therapeutic or merely neutral.
